text: A few jurors smile. Not with you. Grattius smirks openly.
On the tribunal sits the praetor, your own brother Quintus. Eight jurors on the benches. Archias, by your side, does not look up.
Watch who each one will please. Tap a juror to remind yourself what he cares about.
Servius: condemno. He condemns.
A citizen of Heraclea? Then show the court Heraclea's register!
He sang the war against the Cimbri, and pleased even Marius.
Atilius: absolvo. He acquits.
His name is in no census. Not one, in twenty-seven years.
Condemned, by 8 votes to 0. Under the law of Papius, Archias must leave Rome.
Then I shall go where Greek is read. That is everywhere.
The long list of famous friends made Varro yawn.
Metellus was his friend. Of course he wrote him in.
Condemned, by 5 votes to 3. Under the law of Papius, Archias must leave Rome.
A knock. Archias comes in: thin, grey, holding a case of papers as if it might break.
Grattius sits. You have answered him. One more stroke of the law, or leave it there?
Publius: condemno. He condemns.
Gnaeus: condemno. He condemns.

Antioch, where I was born. Fame in Asia and Greece. Tarentum, Rhegium, Neapolis. Rome at seventeen, the year Marius and Catulus were consuls; the Luculli took me in. Heraclea, with Marcus Lucullus. Then the law of 89, and Metellus. Since then, the wars in the east with Lucius Lucullus: I was with his army at the last census, and in Asia at the one before. I have made my will as a Roman, Marcus. I have inherited as one.
How brave, to insult a man who is not here.
While he was still a boy, his talent was famous across all of Asia and Greece.
Convenient absences.
Choose your answer from the evidence you hold: up to three cards, 3 water each.

He sang the war against the Cimbri and the war against Mithridates: our victories, our generals, our name. Greek is read in every nation; through his verse, Rome's glory travels as far as her armies did.
You call your first witness. Marcus Lucullus, senator, rises from the front row. What do you ask him?
The legal chain is there, in order: Rome, Heraclea, the declaration before Metellus. Atilius writes it down.
They say Grattius has the law of Papius in one hand and nothing in the other. But nothing is enough, Marcus, when the papers are ash.
You ask why I love this man? Because he gives my mind rest from the noise of this place, and the strength to speak in it.
So the defence admits it: there is no record. Thank you, Cicero.
The crowd roars before Quintus has finished counting. Archias is a Roman citizen, and everyone in the Forum has heard why poets matter.
Appius' lists were careless, Gabinius' corrupt. But Metellus came to court worried over a single erased name. Look at his lists: there is no erasure over Aulus Licinius.
Each juror takes a wax tablet marked A, absolvo, I acquit, and C, condemno, I condemn; scratches out one letter; and drops it into the urn. Quintus reads them out.

Judges, this man is a Syrian: a Greek who sings for his supper in the houses of the great. He says he is a citizen of Heraclea; then show me Heraclea's register. He says he is a citizen of Rome; then show me his name in one census, any census, in twenty-seven years. You cannot. The law of Papius was made for exactly this man. Send him home.
Tell the jury who he is. Briefly: every part of the story costs water, and only six will fit.
Titus Aufidius: condemno. He condemns.
Choose the parts, in the order you will tell them.
The great Africanus kept the poet Ennius always beside him. Themistocles, asked which voice he liked best to hear, said: the one that best proclaims my deeds.
Most of the class would stop. The jury's faces say something else.
And the other censuses?
I made my will by Roman law. I took inheritances from Roman friends. And at the census of Julius and Crassus, Marcus, nobody was counted at all.
You spoke for poetry, Marcus. Now poetry owes you a poem.
The jury laughs. Then it waits for an ending that does not come: you have finished on a joke.
He never truly lived in Rome. A wandering singer has no fixed home.
He gathers his scrolls slowly. Forty years in this city, and the papers that proved it are ash.
Appius kept his lists carelessly, sir, and Gabinius' were worthless. Metellus? He once came to court worried about a single erased name.
A charming biography. But when, exactly, did this Syrian become a Roman? The defence seems to have forgotten.
Why such love for this little Greek, Cicero? What is a poet to a Roman court?
“I did it myself. I do not think it, I know it. I did not hear of it, I saw it.”
He came to Rome at about seventeen, in the year Marius and Catulus were consuls.
One witness. A friend of the accused, no less.
Enough is a beautiful word, Marcus.
You agree the lists are bad, then?
The defence has nothing to say.
Condemned, by 7 votes to 1. Under the law of Papius, Archias must leave Rome.
Mamilius: condemno. He condemns.

Alexander, standing at the tomb of Achilles, cried out: Fortunate young man, to have found a Homer to sing your courage! Without the Iliad, the same mound that covered his body would have buried his name.
Well? Can you save me?
“It is very fine.” Servius smiles; everyone else waits.
Acquitted, by 5 votes to 3. Not a triumph, but enough. Archias closes his eyes.
Before Grattius replies, you have a moment. Use it?
Sempronius: condemno. He condemns.
These studies nourish youth and delight old age; they adorn good fortune and give refuge and comfort in bad; they please us at home and travel with us, through the night and into the country.
Varro: condemno. He condemns.
“They burned with the record office in the Italian war.”
Three envoys from Heraclea step forward in Greek cloaks and lay a sealed tablet before the praetor: the town's official word that Archias is its citizen.
The room is not sure. Mamilius looks harder at his census lists.
Mamilius: absolvo. He acquits.
The jurors had already made up their minds.
Condemned, by 6 votes to 2. Under the law of Papius, Archias must leave Rome.
Gnaeus: absolvo. He acquits.
You are Marcus Tullius Cicero. Last year you were consul and saved the Republic, or so you like to say. Tomorrow you defend an old man in court.

Ennius calls poets sacred. Rocks and deserts answer a poet's voice. Seven cities quarrel over Homer, a foreigner, each claiming him as its own; and shall Rome drive out a living poet who is hers by law?
Four votes to four. In a Roman court a tie acquits: Archias is saved by the narrowest margin there is. Archias closes his eyes.
When the law of 89 was passed, he declared himself before the praetor Metellus, within the sixty days.
The court is in session. The charge is under the law of Gaius Papius. Grattius, you may speak.
Atilius: condemno. He condemns.
The water is low. One last appeal. How do you end?
Acquitted, by 6 votes to 2. Not a triumph, but enough. Archias closes his eyes.
Did not Pompey himself, our Great one, make his historian Theophanes a Roman citizen in front of his assembled army, while the soldiers cheered?

You have the law, the word of a town, the testimony of Lucullus and the lists of Metellus. Protect, then, a man who has always honoured you, your generals and the Roman people; let him be seen to be rescued by your humanity, not injured by your severity.
Sempronius: absolvo. He acquits.
He was born at Antioch, a rich and famous city, full of learning.
Even if he declared himself, those praetors' lists are worthless. Anyone could buy a line in them.
The room murmurs: absence is not proof. The undecided jurors take note.
That is not an answer to my question.
Varro: absolvo. He acquits.
The law is on your side now. You can see it in Atilius' notes, in Mamilius' nod.
Tarentum, Rhegium and Neapolis made him their citizen, and honoured him.
Servius: absolvo. He acquits.
The Metelli, Catulus, Crassus, Drusus, the Hortensii: the first men of Rome were his friends.
“All Rome knows him.” The jury already knew that.
Titus Aufidius: absolvo. He acquits.
But look at the benches. Varro is checking the sun. Publius is whispering. Titus has folded his arms.
Atilius frowns: the dates of Heraclea and the law came out in the wrong order, and he had to untangle them.
If I have any talent, judges (and I know how little it is), my friend Archias has a right to it. Grant me one favour: let me speak of literature, as befits a poet's defence.

At the last census he was with Lucullus' army; at the one before, in Asia; at the first, no one was counted at all. And a census only shows who claimed citizenship: this man made his will and took inheritances as a Roman.
Rome, 62 BC. Night. A lamp, a table, a hundred scrolls.
The water clock is turned for you. Everyone is looking at you. How do you begin?
The Luculli took him into their house, and it has been his home ever since.

A wretched poet once handed Sulla a few verses in his praise. Sulla paid him at once, on one condition: that he never write anything again. If Sulla rewarded even a bad poet, what would he have given Archias?
Publius: absolvo. He acquits.
“With my brother's army in the east.”
...Forty years in one house. Very well.
It is absurd to say nothing of the proof we have, and demand the proof no one can have.
Most of the class would go on.
With Marcus Lucullus beside him, he was enrolled as a citizen of Heraclea.
He lays the case file on your table. Read it, or don’t: tomorrow you will only have what you know.
You go over the records again. Two jurors are now openly not listening.
Now speak for literature. Choose four arguments, and put them in the order you will make them. 6 water each.
Others spend their free hours on games and dice and parties. I spend mine on books, and from them I come back to the courts stronger, and ready for my friends.
He went east with Lucius Lucullus, and sang the war against Mithridates.
Each question costs water. Ask well.
“I was.”
Keep to the point, Cicero.
Tarentum, Neapolis? Then let Tarentum keep him!
The Forum in spring sunlight. The Rostra, the Temple of Castor, and a crowd that has come to watch a famous man speak.
Witnesses. Always witnesses. Where is the paper?
Heads come up along the benches. The crowd behind them pushes closer.
